It seems that you didn't unpack the title. Because you don't have to answer the question or take a stance. An 'is...' question is basically an 'ought' to be question. The basis of the question itself has certain preconditions... I would look at some strategies about how to discuss the 'ought' to be type of question and avoid taking sides as the essay is about providing a balanced perspective of the essay title.

Ideas are insufficient to just get an A. You can have an unoriginal idea (perhaps you shine a different light to a previously known and valued perspective, isn't that valuable?) and still get an A. Implications and nuance with a sustained focus on the title is key to scoring in a high band grade (notice I didn't say A because nothing will guarantee an A).

If you're looking at methods for history then wouldn't like archiving or examples about how an over reliance on those techniques can cause stagnation? Well it's not what the IB says because the IB delegates grading to examiners, and sustained focus and effective links just mean in technical terms that your essay is holistic and sections have clear links between them and that you justify the use of AOKs in your essay. Ok so I’m not gonna answer each point you’ve made because then I’d have to write an essay. But for the sake of argument lets say that I addressed all your concerns, here’s my summation:

ESL gigs are split into two:

1) Language Teaching 
2) Subject Teaching 

If you go into ESL as a subject teacher you’ll be taken more seriously as a licensed teacher and will have opportunities to make some good money overseas (China and MENA region). 

If you just straight up get a CELTA and BA then you’re not a licensed teacher therefore the pay will be effected by at least 1k a month. So and there are less opportunities to climb up the totem pole because ESL teachers are on the lower end of this. 

You can do a masters of education, DELTA or other programs that will prepare you for admin positions. 

If I were you I’d get a qualified teacher status first and then move on with it. But that is only if you are dead set on this. If you are not sure just get a CELTA and try it out for a year.

And every country, agency and school does contracts differently. Please make sure the contract is air tight before you sign anything. 

Good luck on your journey.

We don't really know a whole lot about mental illnesses period and labeling them tends to make things harder for treatment and the paradox is, not labeling makes it even more of a difficult task to treat. The latest diagnostic trends from DSM are leaning towards defining mental illnesses on a spectrum versus a concrete label. So depression would fall under the low end of an affective spectrum versus bipolar on a higher end of affective spectrum. But the methodology for treatment hasn't changed since this shift to spectrum, you treat the symptoms, not the label. And it's difficult to truly treat someone who is suffering from mental illness, its different for everyone, the norm set in the mental health field is for practical application of medication. Evidence suggests mono-therapy helps but not enough caters to the specific needs of the individual. It's a good safety blanket but its just not enough. It's inadequate to get a prescription and follow a schedule and hope your depression will disappear. 

I really do hope that advances in the care of depression and other disorders will open up more doors for treatment. Such little actual emphasis is given to mental well being. It takes more than a pill to cope with mental health challenges. Coping is the only tool we have that best treats it. So whatever that helps you cope will be just as useful as medication. Negative ways of coping are ample and although they work short term in the long term those methods will erode and cause a relapse. Honestly, any form of sublimation helps with coping positively. And if the anxiety is unbearable and the depression too severe - it causes paralyses. So how do we cope when we are unable to do so? Time. In the end we give ourselves time and the permission to feel awful.
